title: Raising of Re-employment Age at Organisations that Receive Significant Direct or Indirect Government Funding
what_it_is: Raising of Re-employment Age at Organisations that Receive Significant Direct or Indirect Government Funding

sections.label: Raising retirement and re-employment ages
sections.summary: The RA rises to 63 and REA to 68 from July next year, with grants and wage offsets for employers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The recommendations were accepted and we will take the first steps towards achieving this by raising the RA to 63 and the REA to 68 from July next year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding this, the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) encourages all employers to exceed the prevailing statutory retirement age and re-employment age where possible.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We offer the Senior Worker Early Adopter Grant to any employer that implements a higher RA or REA as a company policy, ahead of legislation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Companies can receive up to $125,000 for being early adopters and more than 1,800 companies have already done so.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The public sector has also taken the lead to implement a higher RA and REA ahead of legislation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We also provide wage offsets of up to 8% for employers that hire Singaporean workers aged 55 and above through the Senior Employment Credit scheme which was introduced this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Under the Special Employment Credit scheme that preceded this scheme, the Government provided over $4.6 billion in payments since its inception in 2011.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: For new local hires aged 40 and above, the Jobs Growth Incentive also provides significant wage support of up to $54,000 per hire between September 2020 and September 2021 in eligible firms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This is more than triple the support of up to $15,000 per non-mature hire.
